name: The Loire Valley between Sully-sur-Loire and Chalonnes
description: The Loire Valley stretches along France's last wild river, from Sully-sur-Loire to Chalonnes, and is dotted with riverside towns, vineyards and fairytale châteaux. Its showpiece is Chambord, the valley's largest château, begun in 1519 as a hunting lodge for Francis I. Its Renaissance towers and rooftops rise dramatically from the forest, and about 700,000 people visit each year.
